hook: In 1961, a computer *sang a song* for the first time
caption:
In 1961, a computer sang a song for the first time in history.
The IBM 7094 performed "Daisy Bell (Bicycle Built for Two)" at Bell Labs, marking one of the earliest examples of computer-generated singing.
The machine used speech synthesis to turn digital data into a recognizable human-like singing voice. At the time, computers were mainly used for math and scientific work, making this a remarkable achievement.
The moment even inspired a famous scene in Stanley Kubrick's 1968 film 2001: A Space Odyssey, where the AI computer HAL 9000 sings the same song as it shuts down.
More than 65 years later, AI can generate entire songs, complete with vocals, instruments, and lyrics, in seconds.
And it all started with a computer singing about a bicycle.
